# The Pinocchio (cmeel) stack CI builds against: EXACTLY the set the robot runs.
# Mirror of kinova-gen3-ros2/docker/requirements.txt (the Jetson's pip3 list) --
# keep the two in lockstep. Testing a different Pinocchio than the arm runs is how
# a 3.x-only API (Frame::parentJoint) once passed on the Jetson and failed here.
#
# Pinning `pin` alone is NOT enough. pin 3.9.0's deps are loose ranges, so a
# fresh resolve pulls the newest compatible cmeel packages — but the
# libpinocchio 3.9.0 wheel is built against urdfdom 4, and its DT_NEEDED asks for
# liburdfdom_sensor.so.4.0. Resolving cmeel-urdfdom 6.0.0 therefore produces an
# image that builds fine and then dies at startup with:
#   error while loading shared libraries: liburdfdom_sensor.so.4.0
#
# numpy is deliberately NOT pinned. That host has 1.26.4, but cmeel-boost 1.89.0
# declares numpy>=2.2,<2.3 — the host env predates that constraint and violates
# it, so pip cannot legally reproduce it (ResolutionImpossible). Nothing here
# uses the boost-python/numpy bindings: the node is C++, and the test client only
# needs rclpy. Left to resolve (2.2.x today), and the e2e client run is what
# proves rclpy still imports.
pin==3.9.0
libpinocchio==3.9.0
coal==3.0.2
libcoal==3.0.2
eigenpy==3.12.0
cmeel==0.59.0
cmeel-assimp==6.0.2
cmeel-boost==1.89.0
cmeel-console-bridge==1.0.2.3
cmeel-octomap==1.10.0
cmeel-qhull==8.0.2.1
cmeel-tinyxml2==10.0.0
cmeel-urdfdom==4.0.1
cmeel-zlib==1.3.1
